Fund that contains funding to pay for expenditures not attributed to specific agencies or
departments. This category also includes County-maintained reserves subsequently allocated

Compensation Increases. The FY 2027 Adopted Budget includes funding for compensation
increases as follows: a 4.25 percent merit increase for eligible regular employees on the
general workforce pay plan; a salary scale increase of 2.5 percent and a one-step merit
increase for eligible uniformed Fire and Rescue employees; and a salary scale increase of
5.75 percent and a one-step merit increase for eligible uniformed Sheriff’s deputies. The
general workforce merit increase covers the General Government bargaining unit and
corresponds to the ratified collective bargaining agreement with the Service Employees
International Union (SEIU) Virginia 512. For the Fire and Rescue bargaining unit, this funding
covers the uniformed pay increases and other compensation-related provisions included in
the ratified collective bargaining agreement with the International Association of Fire Fighters
(IAFF) Local 3756. Additional provisions include incremental adjustments to specialty pay and
a 5.5 percent merit increase for employees who are on the general workforce pay plan but
included in the Fire and Rescue bargaining unit. For the Sheriff’s Office, funding is also
included for adjustments to various stipends, including the canine handler stipend, field
training officer stipend, and clothing allowance, to maintain regional competitiveness in line
with the Board’s compensation philosophy.
The FY 2027 Adopted Budget also includes a 2 percent adjustment to the range
minimum and maximum of each grade in the general workforce open range pay plan, which
does not impact employee salaries unless they fall below the adjusted range minimum. In
comparison, salary scale adjustments to public safety grade and step pay plans provide an
additional pay increase to employees by increasing the value of each grade and step.
Salary scale adjustments are budgeted to take effect at the beginning of the fiscal year.
The merit and step increases are budgeted to begin with the second pay period in
September 2026 (paid out with the first paycheck in October). The Board’s approved
compensation philosophy is to deliver pay (average salaries) within a range of 100 to 105
percent of the average mid-point of Loudoun’s comparator market, which is defined as the
Counties of Arlington (VA), Fairfax (VA), Prince William (VA), Montgomery (MD), Frederick
(MD), and Prince George’s (MD); the City of Alexandria; and the District of Columbia. A
summary of recent compensation increases is provided in the tables below.

EMPACT Awards. County policies include provisions to permit individual and team bonus
awards in recognition of outstanding achievement. These provisions are important tools for
supporting an organization that recognizes and rewards excellent performance. Funding for
EMPACT awards in the FY 2027 Adopted Budget has been incrementally adjusted based on
the continued growth of the County workforce.

Personnel Vacancy Savings. The County budgets anticipated savings resulting from
employee turnover in the Non-Departmental budget. This amount is evaluated annually and
adjusted to reflect actual savings, which occur through expenditure balances in departments’
personnel budgets. Personnel vacancy savings are budgeted at a rate of 5.3 percent of salary
and related fringe benefits in the FY 2027 Adopted Budget.

Annual and Sick Leave Payouts. Payout of annual and sick leave balances upon employees’
departures from employment is included in the Non-Departmental budget and allocated to
departments’ personnel budgets as needed throughout the year.

Length of Service Award Program (LOSAP). This is a benefit for volunteer firefighters
previously budgeted in Loudoun County Fire and Rescue’s departmental budget. This
budget is included in the Non-Departmental budget to comply with Governmental
Accounting Standards Board (GASB) statement #73.

Other Post-Employment Benefits (OPEB) Contribution. This represents the County’s
contribution to the OPEB Trust Fund for retiree health insurance benefits. More information
on the County OPEB Trust Fund is available in the Other Funds section.

Retiree Health Insurance. Funding was included to cover expenditures for retiree health
insurance plans on a “pay-as-you-go” basis in the FY 2026 Adopted Budget. For FY 2027, the
OPEB Trust is projected to have sufficient funding for the County to resume withdrawing from
the Trust to cover the County’s share of retiree health insurance costs. Therefore, a separate
allocation for “pay-as-you-go” financing of benefits is not included in the FY 2027 Adopted
Budget.

Hiring Incentive Program. In April 2023, the Board approved amendments to Chapter
252.02, Bonuses, of the Loudoun County Code of Ordinances that authorized the County
Administrator to implement a hiring and retention incentive program. A hiring and retention
incentive program was implemented in April 2024, with the purpose of addressing
challenging recruitment conditions for certain hard-to-fill positions and maintaining
competitiveness with comparator jurisdictions. The FY 2027 Adopted Budget contains
continued funding for this program.

Deferred Compensation Match. The FY 2026 Adopted Budget contained funding to
increase the match for employee contributions to the County’s 457(b) deferred
compensation plan to the greater of $20 or 1 percent of salary per pay period, up to an
annual maximum of $1,000. The increased match has been implemented, and funding was
programmed in department personnel budgets for the FY 2027 Adopted Budget.

Interest Expense. The County budgets interest payments on real and personal property tax
refunds in the Non-Departmental budget.

Payment to Leesburg – Economic Development Payment. At its February 6, 2024
meeting3, the Board reviewed the terms of a mediated agreement and approved the terms of
the agreement, which would allow the Town of Leesburg to annex more than 400 acres of
land known as Compass Creek. As part of the agreement, beginning in FY 2026, the County
will pay Leesburg $2 million (escalated by 3 percent each year) annually to promote
economic development in the Joint Land Management Area outside the town’s limits.

Payment to Nonprofits. This category includes funding provided to nonprofit organizations
through the County’s Human Services Program (including the competitive and core services
provider processes).

Payment to Regional and Intergovernmental Organizations. The County provides
funding to many regional and intergovernmental organizations from which the County
receives operational support. Regional organizations include the Metropolitan Washington
Council of Governments and the Northern Virginia Regional Park Authority, both serving
multi-jurisdictional areas. Intergovernmental organizations include other localities in Loudoun
County, such as the Town of Leesburg, which receives funds to support School Resource
Officers in Leesburg area schools. Beginning in FY 2027, the non-departmental expenditures
pages reflect only contributions budgeted in the non-departmental budget, including salary
supplements. FY 2026 Adopted amounts reflect the incorporation of salary supplements in
the Payment to Regional and Intergovernmental Organizations line. More information can be
found in the Regional and Intergovernmental Organization section.

Payment to the Economic Development Authority (EDA). Beginning in FY 2021, the
County provides funding to the EDA as part of a 15-year incentive to bring the United States
Customs and Border Protection Agency’s Office of Information Technology (OIT) to Quantum
Park in Ashburn. This economic development incentive was agreed to by the Board at the
March 22, 2018 Business Meeting, and payments started on January 1, 2021.

Payment to Loudoun County Public Schools. The FY 2027 Adopted Budget includes a
payment to Loudoun County Public Schools (LCPS) for the local contribution to the school
division. The payment supports the LCPS Operating, Capital Improvement Program (CIP),
and Capital Asset Preservation Program (CAPP) at the following levels.

Resource Requests - One-Time Expenditures (Operating and Capital Outlay). Resource
requests in the FY 2027 Adopted Budget include two types of expenditures: departmental
and non-departmental. Non-departmental costs include those coordinated by other
departments in support of the requests, including the purchase of technology, furniture,
vehicles, and associated office renovations. These non-departmental one-time costs are
centrally budgeted. All one-time capital costs associated with resources added in FY 2027
are planned to be purchased using available FY 2026 budget, hence no capital costs are
shown here.

Legal and Other Contingencies. The category represents contingency funding for potential
outside legal services. Funding from litigation contingency is allocated to the Office of the
County Attorney as needed, subject to Board approval. Additional contingency funds are
budgeted and used on an as-needed basis.

Revenue Stabilization Fund (RSF). In October 2023, the Board of Supervisors adopted
amendments to the Fiscal Policy, including the establishment of the Revenue Stabilization
Fund (RSF). The RSF was established to mitigate revenue shortfalls within a fiscal year directly
attributable to real and business tangible personal property taxes on the data center industry.
The RSF will be refilled and replenished with year-end unassigned fund balance and

Transfer to Children’s Services Act Fund. The Children’s Services Act is funded through a
state pool of monies allocated to each locality, which requires a local match. Annual transfers
are made to this fund to provide for the County’s match.

Transfer to Legal Resource Center Fund. In recent fiscal years, revenues for the Legal
Resource Center Fund (Law Library) have not been sufficient to fund planned expenditures. A
transfer of local tax funding is budgeted to this fund; in the past, a supplemental budget
adjustment of General Fund revenue balanced the revenue shortfall during the fiscal year.

Transfer to Transportation District Fund. The Transportation District Fund was created in
FY 2013 to segregate transportation and transit-related revenues and expenditures. The
County is required to enact a Commercial & Industrial (C&I) Property Tax at $0.125 per $100
valuation or dedicate an equivalent level of funding for transportation and transit purposes to
be eligible to receive the 30 percent share of Northern Virginia Transportation Authority
(NVTA) revenue, as discussed in this document. To date, the Board of Supervisors has taken
no action to levy a C&I Property Tax, and the County dedicates equivalent funding from
general revenues. As state law mandates, this funding is allocated in the Transportation
District Fund, having been transferred from the non-departmental budget of the General
Fund.

Transfer to the Rivana Community Development Authority (CDA) Fund. The Rivana CDA
Fund is established to collect tax increment, special assessment, and special tax collections
on real property for the purpose of paying debts of the authority to finance and construction
public infrastructure at the Rivana at Innovation Station development. Pursuant to the Rivana
Memorandum of Agreement, excess tax revenues above the 2019 assessed values of the
properties within the CDA are to be collected and transferred to the CDA for part of the debt
service needs incurred.

Transfer to Capital Projects Fund. The transfer represents the allocation of local tax funding
sent from the General Fund to the Capital Projects Fund.

Transfer to Capital Asset Preservation Program Fund. The Board established the Capital
Asset Preservation Fund (CAPP) as a consistent means of planning and financing major
maintenance and repair efforts for County facilities. Annual transfers are made to provide
funding for these efforts. Since FY 2023, CAPP also includes the budget for organization-wide
personal computer replacement, formerly part of the General Fund. Additional information is
available in the Other Appropriated Funds section.

Transfer to Major Equipment Replacement Fund. Funding is provided to replace major
equipment valued over $5,000.

Transfer to Debt Service Fund. Local tax funding pays principal and interest on financed
capital improvement projects.

Transfer to Self-Insurance Fund. Risk management and workers’ compensation costs are
funded by annual transfers to the County’s Self-Insurance Fund.

Transfer to Affordable Housing Fund. Local tax funding dedicated to affordable housing
programs is budgeted in the Non-Departmental budget and transferred to the Affordable
Housing Fund. As of FY 2026 Adopted Budget, the amount of recurring local tax funding
support is equivalent to one cent of the real property tax rate, which was increased from the
one-half cent budgeted in previous fiscal years. In the FY 2027 Adopted Budget, this amount
is equivalent to one cent of the real property tax rate ($19.4 million) plus 20 percent of
additional local tax funding available above the 9 percent operating budget growth target
set in budget guidance ($6.6 million).4

Landfill Fee Offsets
July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2028
The County Administrative Support Offset Program (CASOP)1 enables the Board of
Supervisors (Board) to make in-kind contributions to local organizations, governmental
entities, and internal County departments without direct use of local tax funding. The Board
approves landfill fee offsets, recognizing that the Loudoun County Solid Waste Management
Facility, by policy, must recover its disposal operations and Capital Improvement Plan costs
through tipping fees.
Qualifying organizations may request that the Board award them an offset of landfill fees.
The Board awards offsets for two years through the biennial CASOP, provided that
organizations remain in compliance with the criteria for the program and the offset amount is
adopted as part of the annual budget. Applicants must agree to meet all of the following
criteria and adhere to the standards below:
1. The organization must file a written request for an offset by providing all the required
information on the Landfill Fee Offset Award Application Form provided by the
County.
2. The organization must be a governmental entity or nonprofit organization with
Internal Revenue Service 501(c)(3) status.
3. The organization must provide a service for the public good, which must be described
in writing on the Landfill Fee Offset Award Application Form. With regard to 501(c)(3)
organizations, prioritization will be given to organizations that can demonstrate their
services result in savings to the taxpayer and provide a direct benefit to the
community.
4. The organization must agree to ensure that its employees/members do not use the
fee offset for disposal of non-organization generated waste.
5. The organization shall not exceed the offset amount granted by the Board of
Supervisors.
6. The organization must agree to only deliver waste that is generated from within
Loudoun County. Waste must be:
a. Municipal Solid Waste (MSW), Construction Demolition Debris (CDD), or
vegetative waste, in accordance with the Virginia Solid Waste Management
Regulations, the County’s Solid Waste facility Permit(s), facility operational
requirements and the Loudoun County Solid Waste Management Plan
requirements.
b. Non-hazardous.
7. The organization must agree to separate waste as directed by County staff.
8. The organization must agree to follow the posted onsite facility rules and directions
from County staff.

1 Previous budget documents referred to the County Administrative Support Offset Program as the

Landfill Fee Waiver Program.

9. The organization must agree to follow all required pre-authorization protocols for

10. The organization must have a current, active Loudoun County Solid Waste

The total annual landfill fee offset for the FY 2027 Adopted Budget is $1,134,400 which is
consistent with the total amount available identified in the most recent Financial Analysis of
the Landfill Disposal Operations at the Loudoun County Solid Waste Management Facility
(Financial Analysis). The Financial Analysis is completed annually as part of the budget
development process to project the necessary revenue required to meet operational
obligations.
Organizations receiving fee offsets include Loudoun County Government departments,
Towns within the County, fire and rescue volunteer companies, other government entities,
and nonprofit organizations. Approximately 58 percent of the FY 2027 Adopted Budget
offsets are for Loudoun County Government departments and agencies (including Loudoun
County Public Schools), 12 percent for Town governments, less than 1 percent for volunteer
fire and rescue companies, 26 percent for other government entities, and 4 percent for
nonprofit organizations.1
The upcoming fee offset period is from July 1, 2026, through June 30, 2028. The annual
landfill fee offset for FY 2028 is projected to be consistent with the FY 2027 Adopted Budget.

Nonprofit Organizations1
Based on available resources, the County provides funding allocations to community-based
organizations that deliver services with a direct benefit to vulnerable Loudoun County
residents. The FY 2027 Adopted Budget includes an overall allocation of $8,170,573 for
nonprofit organizations through two distinct programs: the Competitive Grant Program2 and
the Core Service Contracts3.

The Board of Supervisors (Board) continues to improve and refine these two programs based
on recommendations from key stakeholders and County staff. These improvements represent
an effort to strengthen the County’s coordination and collaboration with community partners
and to ensure local funds are leveraged in the most effective manner for the County’s most
vulnerable residents.

Competitive Grant Program
The Competitive Grant Program is designed to leverage local funding in the most effective
manner to assist the County’s most vulnerable and disadvantaged residents in meeting
critical health, safety, security, and independence needs. The FY 2027 Adopted Budget
includes $3,958,331 for the program, which is based on the availability of funding resources
and subject to a competitive process. The FY 2026 Adopted Budget included $2,947,966 for
the competitive grant program; however, on May 20, 2025, the Board approved an
additional $895,073 in FY 2025 fund balance to fully fund the recommended nonprofit
organizations, bringing the total allocation to $3,843,039 for FY 2026.4 This additional

For the competitive grant process, a committee of contracted subject matter experts and
the Department of Finance and Procurement review grant applications and develop funding
recommendations for consideration by the Board. On October 13, 2020, the
Finance/Government Operations and Economic Development Committee (FGOEDC)
provided guidance to fund applicants scoring 75 percent or higher in the application review
process.1 Additionally, the FGOEDC provided guidance that a funding gap analysis be
completed each year as part of the process to support budget planning.
The Board also adopted broad Areas of Need categories that focus on the impact or
outcomes that nonprofit programs will have on the community:
•  Prevention and Self-Sufficiency: Services focused on assisting individuals and
families in becoming and/or remaining independent and stable, and providing tools,
skills, strategies, and resources to individuals and families.
•  Crisis Intervention and Diversion: Services provided to individuals and families in
crisis to overcome immediate problems and reduce or prevent further penetration to
more restrictive and expensive higher-level services.
•  Long-Term Support: Services that focus on assisting individuals who have continuing,
long-term support needs to remain healthy, safe, and independent in the community.
•  Improved Quality of Human Services: Services and opportunities provided to
individuals, organizations, and communities that enhance the quality, accessibility,
accountability, and coordination of services provided by community organizations.
In addition to the larger competitive grant process, the Board created a simplified grant
process for mini-grants in amounts up to $5,000. This program involves a simplified
application process for any organization applying for a small grant for the purposes of
capacity building or small-scale innovative ideas or projects. The budget for this mini-grant
program is approximately 3 percent of the total competitive grant process annually and is
deducted from the total competitive grant budget.

Core Service Contracts
Core service providers meet the critical needs of those most vulnerable and disadvantaged in
the community through contracts with the County. With guidance from County
Administration and feedback from the departments of Family Services; Health; Mental Health,
Substance Abuse and Development Services; and Parks, Recreation, and Community
Services, the Department of Finance and Procurement issued requests for proposals for
healthcare services, domestic violence services, independent living services, dental services,
and representative payee services. In FY 2027, the County is anticipated to hold six contracts
for these services that are managed by various departments. The FY 2027 Adopted Budget

Organizations Contributions
Contractual and formulary contributions are made to regional organizations that provide
services on a multi-jurisdictional level on behalf of several localities in the region. Funding is
defined by contractual agreements, and funding requests submitted by each organization
are generally based on a formulary approach. Requests are reviewed by the Office of
Management and Budget. Regional organizations contribute to the economic development,
education, recreation, culture, health, and well-being of the community. Examples include
the Metropolitan Washington Council of Governments (COG), a multi-governmental
organization that supports many of the County’s planning efforts, and the Northern Virginia
Regional Park Authority, a collective effort of Northern Virginia governments to provide
recreational and park opportunities for member jurisdictions. Intergovernmental
contributions are allocated to public entities that provide specific services within their
jurisdiction. The contribution to the Town of Leesburg for school resource officers (SROs) is
considered an intergovernmental contribution. This contribution provides partial funding for
the cost of Leesburg Police SROs located at public middle and high schools located within
the Town of Leesburg.
The FY 2027 Adopted Budget includes an overall allocation of $14,059,413 and local tax
funding in the amount of $12,851,538 for regional and intergovernmental organizations,
which represents an increase of 13 percent compared to the local tax funding for these
contributions in the FY 2026 Adopted Budget. This increase is mostly due to new local tax
funding contributions for regional public safety programs through COG and the Northern
Virginia Emergency Response System that were previously funded through the Urban Area
Security Initiative (UASI) grant from the federal government.
The overall allocation includes $2,397,463 for salary supplements for state employees,
specifically for the Virginia Indigent Defense Commission’s Loudoun Public Defenders Office,

Revolving Loan Fund
On July 21, 1992, the Board of Supervisors (Board) created the Revolving Loan Fund (RLF), a
portion of the County’s non-spendable General Fund balance. The RLF provided a financing
mechanism for capital projects and the equipment needs of general government, the
schools, and volunteer fire and rescue companies. During the CIP deliberation process on
March 21, 1996, the Board redefined the scope of the RLF by limiting entities that may
receive these funds to future non-general government and non-school requests related to
wastewater treatment projects or volunteer/fire and rescue projects. Further, on September
15, 2020, the Board broadened the RLF to “assist other governmental agencies and volunteer
fire and rescue companies within the geographic boundaries of the County.”1

Revenue  An increase in assets or financial resources. Revenue types are from
local sources, from the Commonwealth of Virginia, the Federal
Government, and from Non-Revenue Receipts (other Financing
Sources).
Revolving Loan  A fund established by the Board of Supervisors for County
Fund  government, School, and Fire and Rescue company capital projects.
Loans from the fund must be repaid back into the fund.
Rollback taxes  Amount of the difference between the taxes calculated for a
property with and without the exemption for the previous five years.
Short-Term Debt  Debt with a maturity of less than one year after the date of issuance.
Special District  An independent unit of local government organized to perform a
single governmental function or a restricted number of related
functions. Special districts usually have the power to incur debt and
levy taxes; however, certain types of special districts are entirely
dependent upon enterprise earnings and cannot impose taxes.
Examples of special districts are the Route 28 Special Improvement
District and the Metrorail Service District.
State and Federal  A governmental fund type used to account for the proceeds of
Grant Fund  specific revenue sources (other than for major capital projects) that
are legally restricted to expenditure for specified purposes.
State Compensation A State Board that determines the rate of State funding toward the
Board  total cost of office operations for Constitutional Officers.
Step Increase  An increase in base salary from the dollar amount of one step to the
dollar amount of the next higher step on a grade and step pay plan.
A step increase typically occurs due to a merit increase, which is
approved by the Board.

Task Force  A group of individuals organized to discuss and research a particular
topic. Task forces are often used as advisory groups on a given topic.
Tax Base  The aggregate value of taxed items. The base of the County’s real
property tax is the market value of all real estate in the County. The
base of the personal property is the market value of all automobiles,
trailers, boats, business equipment, etc., which are taxed as personal
property by the County. The tax base of a sales tax is the total
volume of taxable sales.
